target_customer: Career changers, especially women, BIPOC and LGBTQ+ people, paying for an online UX/UI design bootcamp
problem: Design education is expensive and inaccessible, and design teams lack diversity.
business_model: Tuition for a 16 week bootcamp (4,500 dollars list) plus career services with a job guarantee tier, with Affirm financing

founders.name: Maca Baigorria
founders.background_notes: Self taught designer who moved from mechanical engineering to UX/UI per YC page.

founders.name: Alexandra Amico
founders.background_notes: Moved from systems engineering to product management per YC page.

competitors.name: CareerFoundry
competitors.what: Online UX design program with job guarantee

competitors.name: Google UX Design Certificate
competitors.what: Self paced beginner course series on Coursera

technical_complexity.rationale: Delivering cohort based online education needs content and mentors, not hard technology.

defensibility.rationale: Bootcamps are easy to replicate and compete on price and placement claims; cheaper alternatives like the Google certificate exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large providers kept marketing UX programs; no incumbent absorbed Avocademy in sources found.

market_need_then: UX and tech career change demand was high in 2021 and 2022 per UX Planet coverage of the rise of online bootcamps; the company states most students are women and BIPOC but gives no independent outcome data.

branding.brand_signature: Avocado theme with the blog called The Guac
branding.community_and_virality: Site shows Course Report rating 4.81 from 381 reviews and Career Karma 4.8; the avocado name is not explained in any source found.

brand_strength.rationale: A playful, memorable name and consistent avocado theme with strong self reported review volume, but no independent press on the brand.

pivots.to: Added a UX/UI Design for AI Products program
pivots.why: Company site lists a program without the job guarantee; date and reason not stated

outcome_analysis: Avocademy launched its UX/UI foundations program in 2020 and joined YC in Winter 2022 with an inclusion focused positioning. It reports over 300 placements and strong review counts, and added an AI products program. No external funding round, exit or distress is documented, so success or failure cannot be judged and the mid 2020s bootcamp downturn is not discussed in sources found.
notes: CB Insights aggregator lists 500 thousand dollars raised as a convertible note and Village lists seed; Bounce Watch shows a 2022-04-06 seed of unknown amount. These are single aggregator figures so not recorded as rounds. Competitor source_dates are null because the pages seen are undated or from later years; these rivals existed at the time but the pages do not prove it. Founders' education and employers not found. Avocademy outcome claims such as 300 placements and 85 thousand dollar salaries are company reported and unverified; site price lists 4,500 less 500 yet total 2,497, unexplained.
